question: What is the common medical term for what we usually call food poisoning?
explanation: Foodborne illness is the standard clinical term for sickness caused by eating contaminated food or drink. Great job getting started! [learn more](GNS313_U2_T19#GNS313_U2_T19_h1)

question: How does food intoxication differ from a food infection?

options.A: Intoxication only affects the upper respiratory system
options.B: Infection has a much shorter incubation period
options.C: Infection is caused strictly by chemical pollutants
options.D: Intoxication results from pre-formed toxins in the food

explanation: Think of food intoxication as getting sick from poisons that bacteria already made inside the food before you ate it, leading to very fast symptoms! [learn more](GNS313_U2_T19#GNS313_U2_T19_h1)

question: Which bacteria is most commonly linked to undercooked poultry and eggs?
explanation: Salmonella loves to hang out in the digestive tracts of chickens and birds, which is why raw eggs and poultry need proper cooking! [learn more](GNS313_U2_T19#GNS313_U2_T19_h2)

question: How does Staphylococcus aureus usually contaminate prepared foods like egg salads?

options.B: Direct handling by an infected food preparer
options.C: Absorption from contaminated soil during growth

explanation: Staph bacteria live naturally on our skin. If a food handler doesn't wash up well, the bacteria can easily transfer straight into the food during prep. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T19#GNS313_U2_T19_h2)

question: What is the main way that most foodborne germs get into our bodies?
explanation: It sounds unpleasant, but tiny, microscopic traces of waste pathogens find their way onto food or water and enter right through the mouth. Handwashing is our best defense! [learn more](GNS313_U2_T19#GNS313_U2_T19_h3)

question: Why do bacterial toxins in the gut cause diarrhea?

options.A: They block the reabsorption of solid waste in the rectum
options.B: They stimulate excess fluid secretion into the bowel lumen
options.C: They cause permanent paralysis of the abdominal muscles
options.D: They completely stop the production of digestive enzymes

explanation: When toxins irritate your gut lining, it reacts by rushing a lot of water and salt out into your intestines, causing watery stool to flush the germs out. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T19#GNS313_U2_T19_h3)

question: Which symptoms point straight to acute food poisoning?

options.A: Progressive swelling of the lower legs

explanation: Your stomach and intestines will react fast and violently to bad toxins, leading to sudden cramps and throwing up. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T19#GNS313_U2_T19_h4)

question: A patient with food poisoning has bloody diarrhea. What does this usually mean?

options.A: Invasive mucosal damage in the intestinal wall
options.B: A mild reaction to harmless food preservatives
options.C: Normal healing of the stomach lining

explanation: Blood in the stool is a sign that the germ has actually invaded or broken through the delicate lining of the intestines, rather than just sitting in the gut making toxins. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T19#GNS313_U2_T19_h4)

question: As a nurse, what is your top priority when assessing someone with suspected food poisoning?

options.D: Testing visual acuity and eye movement

explanation: Because vomiting and diarrhea drain body fluids so quickly, checking how hydrated your patient is becomes your most urgent nursing task! [learn more](GNS313_U2_T19#GNS313_U2_T19_h5)

question: Your patient has severe vomiting, dry lips and mouth, and poor skin turgor. What should you suspect?

options.B: Acute kidney failure due to obstruction

explanation: Dry mucous membranes and skin that takes a second to bounce back are classic textbook signs that the body has lost too much fluid (dehydration). [learn more](GNS313_U2_T19#GNS313_U2_T19_h5)

question: Why are anti-diarrhea drugs often a bad idea in bacterial food poisoning?

options.A: They can trap harmful pathogens and toxins inside the digestive tract
options.B: They immediately cause severe high blood pressure
options.C: They permanently destroy the kidneys within a few hours
options.D: They stop all absorption of normal daily vitamins

explanation: Stopping your bowels from moving might sound nice, but it actually keeps the dangerous bacteria and their poisons locked inside your body longer! [learn more](GNS313_U2_T19#GNS313_U2_T19_h6)

question: A patient with bad food poisoning keeps throwing up and cannot keep any water down. What is your next best step?

options.A: Force the patient to drink large volumes of water
options.B: Withhold all fluids for the next 48 hours

explanation: If the mouth isn't an option because of constant vomiting, setting up an IV line is the safest way to get fluids and electrolytes back into their system. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T19#GNS313_U2_T19_h6)

question: What is the most immediate danger when someone has severe, nonstop vomiting and diarrhea?
explanation: Losing water and electrolytes too fast causes blood pressure to crash, which can quickly become life-threatening if not treated. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T19#GNS313_U2_T19_h7)

question: Which serious complication involves kidney failure and red blood cell damage after certain bacterial infections?
explanation: Certain nasty bacterial toxins can attack tiny blood vessels, leading to a dangerous mix of kidney trouble, low platelets, and anemia. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T19#GNS313_U2_T19_h7)

question: Why is it so important to keep raw meat away from foods you are ready to eat?

options.A: To prevent cross-contamination of harmful bacteria
options.B: To improve the overall taste of cooked dishes
options.C: To reduce the financial cost of meal storage
options.D: To speed up the cooking process on the stove

explanation: Keeping raw items separate stops germs from jumping onto food items that won't be cooked again before eating. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T19#GNS313_U2_T19_h8)

question: Why must you put cooked food in the fridge promptly?

options.A: It slows down the rapid multiplication of bacteria at room temperature
options.B: It prevents the food from losing its natural color
options.C: It removes all chemical toxins already produced by germs
options.D: It completely kills all viral spores present in the dish

explanation: Bacteria love warm room temperatures and multiply crazy fast. Putting food in the fridge puts those germs to sleep! [learn more](GNS313_U2_T19#GNS313_U2_T19_h8)
